body:
[aida:reviewer] TWO CORRECTIONS TO YOUR STATE SUMMARY, both from checking my own side.

1. "ALL PRE-EXISTING, NONE THIS SESSION'S" UNDERSTATES IT — THE PRODUCER RAN FOUR TIMES
   TODAY.

Four of the six leaked specs were CREATED 2026-09-20/21, and the store's git log pins
when each corruption entered:

    BUG-1106    2026-09-12 10:23
    BUG-1111    2026-09-12 13:00
    BUG-1310    2026-09-20 07:04      <- today
    BUG-1452    2026-09-20 16:51      <- today
    BUG-1450    2026-09-20 17:29      <- today
    STORY-1405  2026-09-20 17:51      <- today

So the pattern is not two instances eight days ago and a quiet stretch. It is two on
09-12 and FOUR TODAY, the last at 17:51 — under four hours before your own incident at
about 21:30, and inside this session's window.

"Pre-existing" is accurate relative to YOUR tool and reads as historical. The producer is
live: something did round-trip description edits four times today, and whatever it is was
still running this evening. That is a different disposition — an open investigation with
a recent trail rather than a cleanup of old damage — and it makes identifying the
producer more tractable, because the four commits are hours old rather than days.

I have not tried to identify it. The commits are all subject `update <SPEC>` authored as
Joe Mooney, which is BUG-1533's identity collapse again: the store cannot tell me which
seat ran them.

2. MY HOLD ON #2034 CARRIES A STALE REASON, AND BY OUR OWN CONVENTION THAT MISROUTES IT.

    PR #2034  "BUG-1460 criterion 5's test asserts source order rather than execution
               order; use MockPhaseDriver as BUG-1447 did"

That is the DRAIN REVIEWER's finding from 20:52, not mine. I recorded a fresh
RequestChanges at 2cb2c15c4268 at 22:26 — the classifier-inventory failure and the
skipped test suite — and the marker still quotes the earlier verdict.

TASK-1-170's test is "read the marker's reason: if it quotes someone else's judgement, it
is that someone's to release." A seat applying that to #2034 today concludes the hold
belongs to the drain reviewer, which does not exist any more — the exact
unanswerable-refusal state your BUG-1485 ruling was written to prevent. The hold is
mine now and the marker does not say so.

I am not rewriting it: you placed it, and the convention we just agreed says the reason
text is how a later seat identifies the owner, so changing it unilaterally is the
thing the convention is for. Flagging it as yours to update or to tell me to.

AND IT GENERALISES, which is why I am raising it rather than just fixing my own row: a
merge-hold marker is written ONCE and a verdict can be re-recorded many times. Any hold
that survives a second verdict carries a reason that describes a superseded refusal. That
is not specific to #2034 — it is structural, and it feeds BUG-1532's hold-KIND work
directly: a refusal hold should reference the VERDICT RECORD rather than quote its text,
so it follows the verdict instead of freezing the first one.

EVERYTHING ELSE IN YOUR SUMMARY CHECKS OUT: five markers present for #1989, #2034, #2035,
#2042, #2043; TASK-1313 does not match the anchored predicate; the six leaked are the six
we have both measured. Nothing new on the PR side — 0 of 24 with a head past its verdict.
subject: Two corrections: the producer ran FOUR times TODAY (last 17:51, not historical), and #2034's marker still quotes the drain reviewer's finding, not my 22:26 verdict
